population.text: More people live inside one circle over South and East Asia, about 4,000 km in radius, than in the rest of the world combined.
By the UN's 2025 count, Jakarta is the world's biggest city at about 42 million people, ahead of Dhaka and Tokyo.
Mongolia is the least densely populated country, with about 2 people per square kilometre.

land.text: Russia alone covers about 11% of the world's land.
Canada has the longest coastline of any country: at least 202,080 km.

rice.text: Rice is the staple food for more than half of the world's people.
About four fifths of the world's rice is grown by small farmers and eaten close to where it grows.

beer.text: Czechia has drunk the most beer per person every year since 1993: about 152 litres each in 2023.

coffee.text: Finns drink the most coffee in the world, about 12 kg of beans per person a year.

tea.text: Türkiye drinks the most tea per person, about 1,300 cups each a year.

wine.text: Vatican City has topped the world for wine per person: about 74 litres each in 2012.
The oldest known winery, found in a cave in Armenia, is about 6,100 years old.

chocolate.text: Côte d'Ivoire grows about 40% of the world's cocoa.
The Aztecs used cocoa beans as money and demanded them as tribute.

bananas.text: Botanically, bananas are berries. Strawberries are not.
Almost every banana traded between countries is one variety: the Cavendish.

potatoes.text: In 1995, five small potatoes were grown on board the Space Shuttle Columbia.

eggs.text: China lays about a third of the world's eggs.

fish.text: In 2022, for the first time, fish farms produced more aquatic animals than wild fishing.
People in the Maldives eat the most fish in the world, more than 80 kg each a year.

earthquakes.text: The strongest earthquake ever recorded hit Chile in 1960, at magnitude 9.5.
The USGS estimates several million earthquakes happen every year. Most are too small or remote to detect.
Japan has 0.28% of the world's land but about 18% of its magnitude 6+ earthquakes.

mcdonalds.text: Iceland has had no McDonald's since 2009. Its last burger and fries are still on display, barely decayed.
Since 1986, The Economist has compared Big Mac prices around the world to judge whether currencies are over or undervalued.

cattle.text: Brazil has more cattle than people.

sheep.text: In 1982 New Zealand had about 70 million sheep, 22 for every person. Today it's under 5.

pigs.text: About half of the world's pigs live in China.

chickens.text: There are more than three chickens for every person on Earth.
Chickens were first domesticated about 3,500 years ago, drawn to the rice fields of Southeast Asia.

goats.text: People herded goats in Iran's Zagros Mountains about 10,000 years ago, making them one of the first farm animals.

brick-kilns.text: Almost everyone in Bangladesh lives within 10 km of a brick kiln.
Brick kilns produce about 17% of Bangladesh's yearly CO2 emissions.

igp-coal.text: Coal makes about three quarters of India's electricity.

igp-cement.text: India makes the second most cement in the world: about 450 million tonnes in 2024, behind China's 1.9 billion.

igp-paper.text: In 105 CE, Cai Lun presented a papermaking process to China's emperor, though simpler paper existed before him.

igp-waste.text: Delhi's Ghazipur landfill was about 65 m tall in 2019, close to the 73 m Taj Mahal.

africa-power.text: Africa has 60% of the world's best solar resources but only about 1% of its installed solar power.
Almost 600 million people in Africa still have no electricity.

africa-waste.text: More than 90% of Africa's waste goes to dump sites, often burned in the open.
19 of the world's 50 biggest dump sites are in Africa.

lake-area.text: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh water.

lakes.text: About 62% of the world's lakes are in Canada (counting lakes of 10 hectares and up).

languages.text: Papua New Guinea has about 840 living languages, more than any other country.

dinosaurs.text: Megalosaurus was the first dinosaur to get a scientific name, in 1824. The word "dinosaur" only came 17 years later.

cassava.text: After rice and maize, cassava is the third biggest source of calories in the tropics.

millet.text: The UN made 2023 the International Year of Millets, after a proposal from India.

sorghum.text: Sorghum is the world's fifth most important cereal, after maize, rice, wheat and barley.

apples.text: China grows nearly half of the world's apples.

sweet-potatoes.text: China grows about 55% of the world's sweet potatoes.

dates.text: Egypt grows more dates than any other country, about 19% of the world's crop.

olive-oil.text: Spain produces more olive oil than any other country.

rye.text: Germany, Poland and Russia grow 57% of the world's rye.

mutton.text: China produces about 31% of the world's sheep meat, more than any other country.
